chunks: Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Sa'd ibn Abdallah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, that he wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)

asking him about Allah, Mighty and Majestic: Did He have knowledge of things before He created the things and brought them into existence, or did He not know that until He created them and intended their creation and formation, so He knew what He created at the moment of creation and what He formed at the moment of formation? He wrote in his handwriting: Allah never ceased to be Knower of the things before He created the things, just as His knowledge of the things after He had created the things.
ai.seo_question: Did Allah know creation before He created it?
ai.summary: In this foundational hadith from Al-Kafi, Ayyub ibn Nuh queries Imam al-Rida (AS) regarding the temporal relationship between Divine Knowledge and creation, specifically whether God knew entities before bringing them into existence. The Imam’s concise response affirms that Allah’s knowledge is eternal and unchanging, identical in nature whether considered prior to or subsequent to creation, thereby refuting the notion that knowledge emerged with creation. This establishes the Shia theological position of 'Sifat al-Ilm' as an eternal attribute of God, distinct from the contingent nature of created things.
